subject: Competitive parity fund request and operational playbook
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Clark <emma.clark@rivalhealth.com>
Cc: procurement@rivalhealth.com
Date: 2026-10-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Competitive parity fund request and operational playbook

Hi Emma + procurement team,

Thanks for the time during yesterday's demo. As discussed, RivalHealth is running a head-to-head evaluation that will compare Redwood against their incumbent provider for real-time triage and discharge summaries. You mentioned the incumbent is offering a trial pool that effectively subsidizes the evaluation — to keep this a level playing field we'd like to propose a parity-style trial top-up.

What we're proposing: a conditional credit of $20,000 USD applied to the RivalHealth evaluation project (deal RH-4712) specifically for the head-to-head period. Conditions:
- Credits are for inference usage only (tokens/embeddings).
- Trial runs must complete within 60 days of the start date.
- We require a short mutual action plan and one technical contact for a kickoff.

I've attached a short parity proposal and an operational playbook that maps the trial milestones and acceptance criteria (attachment: parity_proposal.pdf, trial-plan.xlsx). If this structure works, we can fast-track approval with Finance and get a DocuSign ready for signatures.

Next steps I suggest:
1) You confirm the evaluation window and technical POC.
2) I loop in Finance for credit approval and we ship the DocuSign.
3) Technical kickoff within 3 business days of execution.

Would you like me to scope the specific usage cap by dataset / scenario? Happy to tailor.

Best,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-10-12T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Competitive parity fund request and operational playbook

Hi Lauren,

Thanks — the proposal looks reasonable at a high level. A couple of asks from procurement before we route this internally:
- Can you provide a short justification / comparable sheet that explains how the $20k number maps to expected token usage and run scenarios?
- Procurement wants to see terms that prevent credits from being used against unrelated production workloads.

Devon (our ML lead) is copied — he may have follow-ups on the trial acceptance tests. If you can send a brief usage estimate and the proposed DocuSign language we can push this through our internal legal/procurement queue.

—Emma

Head of Partnerships, RivalHealth
emma.clark@rivalhealth.com

Emma / procurement —

Attached is a short usage breakdown and the proposed DocuSign clause that ties credits to the evaluation project (see "Scope of Eval Credits" on page 1). TL;DR: our model of 1.2M tokens/month for typical triage batches maps to ~$18k of inference spend over 45 days; we rounded to $20k to give headroom for parallel tests.

I've also put an operational playbook in the Excel that breaks the run into four gated milestones: ingest, model run, QA sweep, acceptance. Credits are released at milestone boundaries to reduce risk and ensure progress.

Marcus — can Finance give a quick read and signal if this is approvable without exec review? We're aiming for no delays — Rival wants the kickoff week of Oct 19.

Thanks,
Lauren

(attachment: trial-usage-estimates.pdf)
(attachment: docusign-draft.txt)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-10-14T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Competitive parity fund request and operational playbook

Lauren / Vivek —

Reviewed the usage estimates. Finance is comfortable approving an up-to-$25,000 conditional credit for RivalHealth for the stated evaluation (deal RH-4712) on the following conditions:
- Credits applied only to the evaluation project namespace (we will create a dedicated API key and project ID).
- Credits expire 90 days after activation.
- RivalHealth signs the standard Trial Credit Agreement and returns a countersigned DocuSign.
- Technical kickoff and milestone gating must be documented in the playbook (we saw that in the Excel; good).

I'm attaching the approval stamp for records (attachment: credit-approval-stamp.pdf). Lauren, you can proceed to generate the DocuSign envelope and send. If Rival asks for a higher amount, escalate to me with expected ROI / reference customers.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Finance Operations | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com

(attachment: credit-approval-stamp.pdf)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Clark <emma.clark@rivalhealth.com>, procurement@rivalhealth.com
Cc: marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-10-15T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Competitive parity fund request and operational playbook

Emma / Procurement —

Great — we can confirm the following and are ready to execute:
- Redwood will provide up to $25,000 in evaluation credits (conditional, see Marcus's note) tied to deal RH-4712.
- We will provision a dedicated project namespace and one evaluation API key; credits will only be usable in that namespace.
- Credits expire 90 days after activation.
- DocuSign link for the Trial Credit Agreement: https://www.docusign.com/links/RH-4712-sign

Please review the DocuSign and the trial-plan spreadsheet. Once countersigned we'll schedule a 30-minute technical kickoff with Devon and our solutions engineer to map the data pipes and acceptance tests. Suggested kickoff window: Oct 20–22.

If procurement needs alternate wording on the scope, loop in legal and we can do a redline pass. Looking forward to running this — we think Redwood's latency and prefix caching will be a strong differentiator for the triage scenario.

Best,
Lauren
